tagline: Regional airline operator providing scheduled passenger service under code-share agreements
hero_kpi_rationale: Financial pillar representing 84.3% of operating revenue, generated by capacity agreements with major airline partners

kpis.name: Capacity Purchase Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from capacity purchase agreements with major airline partners
kpis.description: Revenue generated from capacity purchase agreements where major airline partners pay fixed rates based on completed flights, flight time and aircraft under contract
kpis.signal: Significant increase driven by higher block hours and increased aircraft utilization due to improved captain availability

kpis.name: Prorate Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from prorate agreements and on-demand charter services (SWC)
kpis.description: Revenue from agreements where company shares passenger fares with major airline partners and controls scheduling/pricing on certain routes; includes on-demand charter revenue
kpis.signal: Strong growth from higher passenger numbers and increased prorate/charter flights; company bears operating costs and shares passenger revenues

kpis.name: Total Block Hours
kpis.explanation: Total flight hours measured from takeoff to landing including taxi time
kpis.description: Total block hours (takeoff to landing including taxi) representing primary driver of capacity purchase agreement revenue
kpis.signal: Significant increase driven by improved captain availability enabling higher aircraft utilization and scheduled daily departures

kpis.name: Passengers Carried
kpis.explanation: Total number of passengers transported during the period
kpis.description: Total passengers carried representing primary driver of revenue under prorate agreements with major airline partners
kpis.signal: Solid growth from increased flight operations and higher aircraft utilization; primary driver of prorate agreement revenue

kpis.name: Fleet Size
kpis.explanation: Total number of aircraft in the operating fleet
kpis.description: Total number of aircraft in fleet including scheduled service, leased to third parties, and spare aircraft supporting code-share agreements
kpis.signal: Slight net increase reflecting fleet modernization with E175 additions and older CRJ aircraft removals

risks.title: Dependence on Code-Share Agreements with Major Airline Partners
risks.score_rationale: Code-share agreements represent the core business model, with capacity purchase revenue alone representing 84.3% of flying agreement revenues. Contract termination or renegotiation could materially impact revenue stability and operations

risks.title: Volatility in Maintenance and Fuel Costs
risks.score_rationale: Operating expenses increased 13.4% YoY while revenue grew 15.0%, with capacity purchase agreements providing fuel reimbursement but prorate agreements exposing company to fuel price volatility. Fleet age and increased utilization drive maintenance pressures

risks.title: Fleet Modernization Transition and Integration Risks
risks.score_rationale: Company undergoing significant fleet changes with E175 additions (8 aircraft in 2025, 9-10 additional planned for 2026) and CRJ aircraft phase-outs. Delivery delays, integration challenges and removal of older high-maintenance aircraft create operational risks

risks.title: Labor Availability and Pilot Shortage Constraints
risks.score_rationale: Captain availability was a binding constraint in 2024 but less restrictive in 2025, allowing 14.7% increase in block hours. However, future growth remains dependent on pilot labor availability. Salary pressures evident in 6.5% increase in personnel costs

risks.title: Prorate Agreement Revenue Volatility and Operating Cost Exposure
risks.score_rationale: Prorate revenue grew 33.5% to $607M (15.7% of flying agreement revenue), but exposes company to passenger traffic fluctuations, fuel price volatility, and airport cost variations while bearing full operating costs

risks.title: Passenger Load Factor Compression
risks.score_rationale: Passenger load factor declined from 82.8% in 2024 to 81.5% in 2025 (1.3 percentage point decline) despite 8.7% passenger growth, indicating potential pricing pressure or demand softness that could impact prorate revenue quality

ai_positioning.summary: SkyWest does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing
